rows.subtype: Frown, scowl and pout in frustration [Expressing]
rows.description: A toddler frowns, scowls or pouts when a toy is taken or a wish is refused, signalling frustration or a wish to be comforted rather than deliberate manipulation. Naming the feeling helps the child learn it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Grimace and wince at pain or taste [Expressing]
rows.description: A toddler grimaces at a bitter taste or winces after a bump, a mostly reflexive signal of discomfort. Adults read it together with the situation and check for real injury instead of assuming a tantrum.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler stares with an open mouth at a new animal or a sudden noise, which can mean wonder, startle or the start of fear. A caregiver's calm face helps the child decide which it is.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, curiosity, surprise, calm

rows.subtype: Smile and beam as social signal [Expressing]
rows.description: A toddler beams at a familiar caregiver, showing delight and attachment; the smile is often a reflex-turned-social response and does not yet mean the child is hiding or planning anything.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young infant or toddler gives a broad open-mouth smile to a familiar face, showing pleasure and connection. Responding with a smile back builds the early conversation of attention.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Sustained and fleeting smiles in play [Expressing]
rows.description: A toddler flashes a fleeting smile at a peekaboo surprise and a sustained one during a favourite game, showing joy that rises and fades quickly. Short smiles are normal and not a sign of disinterest.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, interest, surprise

rows.subtype: Brow raise in surprise and attention [Expressing]
rows.description: A toddler raises both eyebrows at a new sight or a sudden funny sound, showing surprise or interest. It is an early, fairly universal signal and mostly reflexive.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, interest, surprise

rows.subtype: Furrowed brow in effort or upset [Expressing]
rows.description: A toddler furrows the brow while concentrating on stacking blocks or before crying, meaning effort, confusion or distress. Adults check the situation and offer help instead of assuming anger.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: sadness, anger, confusion

rows.description: A toddler squeezes the eyes shut when scared, tired or refusing to look, and blinks slowly when sleepy. These are protective or tired signals, not defiance.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: hostility, fear, tiredness

rows.subtype: Wide eyes in wonder and fear [Expressing]
rows.description: A toddler widens the eyes at something new, which can mean fascination or alarm. Looking at the caregiver for a reaction, called social referencing, helps decide which.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, curiosity, awe
